newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania says OSCE mission not likely to arrive.
newsitem.headline: Albania says OSCE mission not likely to arrive.

text.p: The Albanian government has made no agreement with the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) for it to send a fact-finding mission to the country, government sources said on Wednesday.

The OSCE said on Tuesday it had asked former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky to travel to Albania as soon as possible to assess the situation in the troubled Balkan nation, where a state of emergency has been declared.
"There has never been an agreement in principle by the Albanian government to let that mission come," the government source said.
An OSCE spokeswoman said the mission from the 53-state body grouping Europe with the United States and Canada was to leave on Thursday but the timing had been put in question.
A Western diplomatic source said the OSCE was still in talks with the Albanian government and hoped to reach an agreement.
"They've agreed to it, so they just can't say 'no' now," the source said.
But the Albanian government source said the statement by the diplomatic source was incorrect. "It is very likely that the mission will not come," the source said.
